correctness.rationale: Every diameter-three tree has a central adjacent pair, and all other vertices are leaves adjacent to one of the pair. Anchor the Gram matrix at the first hub. Leaf contrasts each have eigenvalue q/2. In coordinates consisting of the unanchored hub and the two leaf totals, the hub pivot is 1, its couplings are (2−q)/2 and q/2, and the leaf block has diagonal 1−q/2+q/(2m), q/2+q/(2n), and off-diagonal (1+q−q^s)/2. The hub Schur complement has diagonal q(2+2/m−q)/4, q(2+2/n−q)/4 and off-diagonal −(2q^s−2−q²)/4. For S=m+n>2 the latter numerator F increases on [2,3] since s>19/12>3^(5/12)>3^(2−s); q√(A_m A_n) strictly decreases on [2,2+2/max(m,n)), by the logarithmic derivative bound 1/2−S/4<0. They cross once before the first diagonal can vanish. Rank is one in the complement at the crossing; above it the determinant first becomes negative, and for q>2+2/max(m,n) a diagonal is negative. Strict nesting supplies all p<1, with p=0 elementary. The path exception embeds in a line at p=2, and no higher power can satisfy the snowflake triangle inequality along three successive vertices. At q_0=2+2/S, midpoint convexity at 2,3,4 gives F(q_0)<2/S, while q_0√(A_m A_n)=2q_0/S; every root lies above q_0. There A_m A_n=(q−2)^2+[4−2S(q−2)]/(mn) strictly increases with mn while the admissible q interval only widens as the larger leaf count decreases. This proves strict balancing. Substitution at m=n and differentiation in 1/m give the stated asymptotic. Frozen code and notes were inspected, not run. The separately written `python /workspace/branches/independent_reproduction.py 3` passed 72 independent shortest-path Gram instances (all unordered splits for 2≤m+n≤17), including endpoint nullity and sample fixed-sum monotonicity; the proof does not extrapolate the sample.
